# Data Dictionary

All data in this project is synthetically generated. This document defines every field in every dataset and every engineered feature used by the models.

---

## Dataset 1: Returns Dataset (`data/raw/returns.csv`)

This is the primary dataset for Phase 1 (Return Risk Scorer).

### Raw Fields (generated by `data/generate_data.py`)

| Field | Type | Description | Example |
|-------|------|-------------|---------|
| `return_id` | string | Unique identifier for the return request | `R_00001` |
| `order_id` | string | Unique identifier for the original order | `O_48291` |
| `customer_id` | string | Unique identifier for the customer | `C_10042` |
| `merchant_id` | string | Unique identifier for the merchant | `M_5021` |
| `product_category` | string | Category of the product being returned | `electronics`, `apparel`, `books`, `home`, `luxury` |
| `order_value` | float | Value of the original order in INR | `14999.00` |
| `order_date` | date | Date the original order was placed | `2024-03-15` |
| `return_request_date` | date | Date the return was requested | `2024-03-28` |
| `return_reason` | string | Self-reported reason for the return | `defective`, `wrong_item`, `not_needed`, `quality_issue`, `changed_mind` |
| `payment_method` | string | How the original order was paid | `card`, `upi`, `netbanking`, `wallet`, `cod` |
| `support_contacted` | boolean | Did customer contact support before returning? | `True`, `False` |
| `images_submitted` | boolean | Did customer submit product images with return? | `True`, `False` |
| `customer_total_orders` | integer | Total orders placed by customer (lifetime) | `23` |
| `customer_total_returns` | integer | Total returns made by customer (lifetime) | `18` |
| `customer_account_age_days` | integer | Days since customer account was created | `412` |
| `customer_returns_30d` | integer | Returns made by customer in last 30 days | `3` |
| `customer_orders_30d` | integer | Orders placed by customer in last 30 days | `4` |
| `is_label_abusive` | boolean | **Target variable** — was this return actually abusive? | `True`, `False` |

---

### Notes on the Target Variable

`is_label_abusive = True` means the return was one of:
- Wardrobing (product worn/used before return)
- Swap fraud (wrong or broken product returned)
- Refund fishing (claimed non-delivery of delivered item)
- Serial return (customer's lifetime return rate > 70%)

In the real world, this label would come from manual review teams or post-return investigation. In our synthetic data, it is generated based on rules that approximate these patterns.

## Dataset 2: Transactions Dataset (`data/raw/transactions.csv`)
**Used in Phase 2 (Fraud Transaction Scorer)**

| Field | Type | Description | Example |
|-------|------|-------------|---------|
| `transaction_id` | string | Unique transaction identifier | `T_00001` |
| `customer_id` | string | Customer identifier | `C_10042` |
| `merchant_id` | string | Merchant identifier | `M_5021` |
| `amount` | float | Transaction amount in INR | `8499.00` |
| `transaction_timestamp` | datetime | When the transaction occurred | `2024-03-15 14:32:00` |
| `payment_method` | string | Payment method used | `card`, `upi`, `wallet` |
| `card_bin` | string | First 6 digits of card number (BIN) | `411111` |
| `card_country` | string | Country of card issuer | `IN`, `US`, `GB` |
| `device_fingerprint` | string | Hashed device identifier | `d8f3a1c2` |
| `ip_address` | string | IP address of transaction | `103.21.45.12` |
| `ip_country` | string | Country resolved from IP | `IN`, `SG`, `US` |
| `billing_pincode` | string | PIN code from billing address | `560001` |
| `shipping_pincode` | string | PIN code from shipping address | `400001` |
| `is_new_device` | boolean | Device seen for first time | `True`, `False` |
| `is_international_card` | boolean | Card issued outside India | `True`, `False` |
| `account_age_days` | integer | Customer account age at transaction time | `8` |
| `is_label_fraud` | boolean | **Target variable** — was this transaction fraudulent? | `True`, `False` |

## Engineered Features

These are computed from the raw fields during feature engineering (`src/features.py`). These are what the model actually trains on — not the raw fields directly.

### Return Risk Features

| Feature | Formula / Logic | Why It Matters |
|---------|----------------|----------------|
| `return_rate_lifetime` | `customer_total_returns / customer_total_orders` | High lifetime return rate = serial returner |
| `return_rate_30d` | `customer_returns_30d / customer_orders_30d` | Recent abuse pattern (more current than lifetime) |
| `days_to_return` | `return_request_date - order_date` (in days) | Very fast (same day) or near-deadline returns are suspicious |
| `is_near_deadline` | `days_to_return >= (policy_days - 2)` | Returning right at the last moment = calculated behavior |
| `is_same_day_return` | `days_to_return <= 1` | Could indicate wardrobing or buyer's remorse abuse |
| `category_risk_score` | Lookup table by `product_category` | Electronics and luxury = higher swap fraud risk |
| `is_first_order` | `customer_total_orders == 1` | No history to validate legitimacy |
| `is_new_account` | `customer_account_age_days <= 30` | New accounts used for one-time fraud |
| `no_images_high_value` | `images_submitted == False AND order_value > 5000` | High-value returns without evidence |
| `no_support_contact` | `support_contacted == False` | Legitimate issues usually involve support first |
| `return_reason_risk` | Encoded value by `return_reason` | "changed_mind" at high value = riskier than "defective" |
| `order_value_normalized` | `order_value / customer_avg_order_value` | Is this return unusually high-value for this customer? |

---

### Fraud Transaction Features

| Feature | Formula / Logic | Why It Matters |
|---------|----------------|----------------|
| `velocity_1h` | Transactions by this customer in last 1 hour | Rapid-fire orders = stolen card being used quickly |
| `velocity_24h` | Transactions by this customer in last 24 hours | Sustained unusual activity |
| `is_address_mismatch` | `billing_pincode != shipping_pincode` | Fraudster ships to their address, not cardholder's |
| `is_new_device` | Device not seen before for this customer | Account takeover or new fraudster device |
| `is_country_mismatch` | `card_country != ip_country` | Card from India but purchase from Singapore = suspicious |
| `amount_vs_avg` | `amount / customer_avg_transaction_amount` | Unusually high order for this customer |
| `account_age_days` | Days since account creation | Very new account placing expensive order |
| `is_prepaid_card` | Derived from `card_bin` lookup | Prepaid cards are harder to trace |
| `is_international_card` | `card_country != 'IN'` | Higher fraud risk for Indian merchants |
| `hour_of_day` | Hour extracted from `transaction_timestamp` | Fraud spikes at certain hours (3–5 AM) |

---

## Risk Level Mapping

| Score | Risk Level | Interpretation |
|-------|-----------|----------------|
| 0.0 – 0.30 | LOW | Likely legitimate, auto-approve |
| 0.30 – 0.70 | MEDIUM | Borderline, flag for human review |
| 0.70 – 1.0 | HIGH | Likely abusive, require evidence or reject |

These thresholds are configurable. See [Evaluation Strategy](evaluation-strategy.md) for how thresholds are chosen.

---

## Categorical Encodings

### Product Category Risk Scores

| Category | Risk Score | Reason |
|----------|-----------|--------|
| `luxury` | 0.9 | High swap fraud — fakes substituted for originals |
| `electronics` | 0.8 | High swap fraud — broken items returned in new packaging |
| `apparel` | 0.6 | Wardrobing common |
| `home` | 0.4 | Lower abuse rates |
| `books` | 0.2 | Very low abuse rates |

### Return Reason Risk Scores

| Reason | Risk Score | Reason |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| `not_needed` | 0.8 | Buyer's remorse — often used to mask wardrobing |
| `changed_mind` | 0.7 | Same as above |
| `quality_issue` | 0.5 | Ambiguous — sometimes legitimate, sometimes swap fraud |
| `wrong_item` | 0.4 | Could be merchant error (lower abuse signal) |
| `defective` | 0.3 | Legitimate claim — easiest to verify with photos |

---

## Data Quality Notes

- All data is synthetic. Distributions are designed to approximate real-world patterns but are not derived from real merchant data.
- Class imbalance is intentional: ~15% abusive returns, ~0.5% fraudulent transactions. This reflects realistic base rates.
- Missing values are introduced intentionally in some fields (e.g., `images_submitted` is null when return reason is "not_needed") to make the dataset realistic.
